rationale: Neither candidate surfaces the ground truth's core technical bugs (stream-slot leak on abort, cumulative/delta rewind, ceil-division length bug, legacy-checkpoint v2-tokenizer mismatch), so recall is low for both. Y is more rigorously grounded, backing nearly every claim with concrete grep evidence and line numbers, and independently catches a genuinely subtle bug (pipeline.py:97 hardcoded stop_token_ids duplicating a config default) plus three well-evidenced test-coverage gaps that echo reviewers' implicit concern about untested new streaming machinery. X makes some unverified 'already handled' claims (slot-leak cleanup, vendored headers) that read as assertions rather than grep-verified facts, slightly undercutting its precision relative to Y's evidence-heavy style.
